title: Genoese Ravioli
instructions:
Genoese Ravioli

Genoese ravioli filled with escarole, borage, sweetbread, spinal marrow, veal, pork, and sausage, served with meat sauce.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

For the pasta
5 cups flour
2 large eggs
1–1 1/4 cups water
2/3 tsp fine salt

For the filling
about 6 cups raw escarole
about 4 cups raw borage
about 1 cup cooked sweetbread
1/4 cup cooked spinal marrow
3 tbsp butter
about 1/4 lb veal
about 1/4 lb lean pork
1/3 cup crumbled sausage
4 large eggs
soft crumb from 1 small bread roll
1/2 cup finely grated Parmigiano
1 tsp finely chopped fresh marjoram
1 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

For serving
2 1/2 cups hot meat sauce
2/3 cup finely grated Parmigiano

For cooking
6 1/3 qt water
2 tbsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Remove the tough leaves from the escarole and borage.

2. Wash the greens and boil them in a very small amount of salted water for 5 minutes.

3. Drain, squeeze very dry, and chop finely.

4. Melt the butter in a saucepan.

5. Add the veal, pork, and sausage and brown for 8–10 minutes.

6. Cool slightly, then mince the meats with the sweetbread and spinal marrow.

7. Moisten the bread crumb with 1/4 cup meat juices or broth and squeeze lightly.

8. Combine the meats, greens, eggs, bread, Parmigiano, marjoram, salt, and pepper.

9. Mix with a wooden spoon until compact.

10. Make the pasta by kneading the flour, eggs, salt, and gradually added water for 10–12 minutes.

11. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.

12. Roll two thin sheets.

13. Place small mounds of filling on one sheet.

14. Cover with the second sheet, press out the air, and seal carefully.

15. Cut the ravioli with a fluted pastry wheel.

16. Air-dry for about 2 hours.

17. Bring the salted water to a boil.

18. Cook the ravioli in small batches for 3–4 minutes after the water returns to a boil.

Service

Drain gently and dress with meat sauce and Parmigiano.

Chef's note

The filling should be flavorful but dry. Thoroughly squeezed greens and cooled meats help prevent the ravioli from opening while cooking.

Picagge with Pesto

Wide Ligurian egg pasta with basil, pine nut, Pecorino, and Parmigiano pesto.

4. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.

6. Let the sheet dry for about 30 minutes.

7. Cut into ribbons about 5/8 inch wide.

8. For the pesto, pound the basil and coarse salt in a mortar.

9. Add the pine nuts, then the garlic and cheeses.

10. Work in the olive oil gradually until creamy.

12. Cook the picagge for 3–5 minutes.

13. Reserve the pasta water.

14. Loosen the pesto with about 1/4 cup pasta water.

Picagge are wider than ordinary tagliatelle, so keeping the pasta sheet thin prevents them from becoming heavy once coated with pesto.

title: Mesciua
instructions:
Mesciua

La Spezia soup of chickpeas, cannellini beans, and farro, finished with extra-virgin olive oil and black pepper.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

1 1/2 cups dried chickpeas
1 1/2 cups dried cannellini beans
1/2 cup farro or wheat berries
1/4 tsp baking soda for soaking
3 1/4 qt water for the chickpeas and farro
2 1/8 qt water for the beans
1 2/3 tsp fine salt, divided
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Put the cannellini beans in a bowl with plenty of warm water and half of the baking soda.

2. In a second bowl, soak the chickpeas and farro in warm water with the remaining baking soda.

3. Soak everything for at least 12 hours.

4. Drain and rinse thoroughly.

5. Put the chickpeas and farro in a pot with the measured water and about 2/3 teaspoon salt.

6. Bring to a boil and cook over low heat for at least 2 hours, until the chickpeas are tender.

7. In a second pot, cook the cannellini beans in their water with about 1/2 teaspoon salt for about 90 minutes.

8. Add the cannellini beans and some of their liquid to the chickpea-and-farro pot.

9. Adjust the total liquid to about 6 1/3 cups.

10. Add the remaining salt and cook everything together for another 15 minutes.

Service

Divide among 6 bowls and finish with extra-virgin olive oil and black pepper.

Chef's note

Cook the legumes separately because chickpeas and cannellini have different cooking times. Combine them only at the end so each keeps the right texture.

title: Genoese Baked Rice
instructions:
Genoese Baked Rice

Genoese baked rice with sausage, peas, artichoke, mushrooms, tomato, Parmigiano, and breadcrumbs.

Yield: 4 servings

2 cups rice
about 7/16 lb fresh sausage, casing removed
1 1/2 cups peas

1 ripe tomato, peeled and seeded
1/2 onion, finely chopped
3 1/2 tbsp butter
6 1/3 cups hot broth
2/3 cup finely grated Parmigiano, divided
1/2 cup breadcrumbs
1 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Soak the dried mushrooms in warm water for 30 minutes.

2. Drain, squeeze, and chop coarsely.

3. Melt the butter in a saucepan.

4. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes.

5. Add the crumbled sausage and brown for 5 minutes.

6. Add the peas, artichoke, mushrooms, and tomato.

7. Add 1/2 cup broth, salt, and pepper.

8. Cover and cook over low heat for 20 minutes.

9. Meanwhile, boil the rice in salted water for about 8 minutes.

10. Drain while very al dente and transfer to the sauce.

11. Add half of the Parmigiano and about 3 cups plus 3 tablespoons hot broth.

12. Transfer to a buttered baking dish.

13. Bake at 350°F for 15 minutes.

14. Mix the breadcrumbs with the remaining Parmigiano.

15. Scatter over the surface and bake for another 5–7 minutes, until golden.

Service

Rest for 5 minutes and serve hot.

Chef's note

The rice goes into the oven very al dente with plenty of broth, which finishes the cooking without drying it out.

Gnocchi with Pesto

Ligurian potato gnocchi with pesto Genovese.

Chestnut Trofie with Pesto

2. Form a well and add the salt.

3. Gradually add the warm water.

5. Cover and rest for 15 minutes.

8. Roll each piece under your palms and drag it across your palm or the work surface to create the twisted shape.

9. Bring the salted water to a boil.

10. Cook the trofie for about 5 minutes, until they float and are cooked through.

11. Drain gently.

Service

Dress with pesto away from direct heat and serve immediately.

Chef's note

Chestnut flour makes the dough more fragile than classic trofie dough. Avoid adding too much water or pressing too hard while shaping.

Bigoli in Salsa

Venetian bigoli with slowly stewed onions, anchovies, white wine, and parsley.

4. Add the chopped anchovies.

5. Stir over low heat until they dissolve completely.

instructions:
Bigoli with Duck Ragù

Venetian bigoli with white duck ragù, soffritto, white wine, juniper, rosemary, and bay.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

1 1/3 lb duck meat, finely chopped

For cooking
5 1/4 qt water
1 tbsp plus 2 tsp fine salt
2 tbsp pasta cooking water to reserve

Preparation

1. Finely chop the onion, carrot, and celery.

2. Trim any obvious sinew from the duck and chop it finely by hand.

3. Heat the olive oil with half of the butter in a saucepan.

4. Add the vegetables and garlic and cook for 10 minutes.

5. Add the duck and brown for about 8 minutes.

6. Add the rosemary, bay leaves, whole clove, and juniper.

7. Season with salt and pepper.

8. Pour in the wine and let it evaporate.

9. Remove the garlic.

10. Add about 1 cup broth.

11. Cover partially and simmer for 75–80 minutes; after 25 minutes add half of the remaining broth, and after 50 minutes add the final half.

12. Remove the whole herbs and spices.

13. Bring the salted cooking water to a boil.

14. Cook the bigoli for 8–10 minutes.

15. Reserve the pasta water and drain.

16. Transfer the bigoli to the ragù.

17. Add the remaining butter and pasta water.

18. Toss for 1 minute.

Service

Divide among 4 plates and finish with Grana if desired.

Chef's note

This is a white ragù: the duck flavor is concentrated with broth, wine, and aromatics rather than tomato.

title: Risi e Bisi
instructions:
Risi e Bisi

Classic Venetian rice and peas with pancetta, onion, parsley, butter, and Parmigiano.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

1 1/2 cups Carnaroli rice
2 1/2 cups peas
6 1/4 cups hot vegetable broth
1/3 cup diced pancetta
1/2 white onion, finely chopped
3 1/2 tbsp butter, divided
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1/4 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
1/4 cup finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano
3/4 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Keep the broth at a gentle simmer.

2. Melt about 1 1/2 tablespoons butter with the olive oil in a saucepan.

3. Add the pancetta, half of the onion, and half of the parsley.

4. Cook for 5 minutes.

5. Add the peas and about 1/3 teaspoon salt.

6. Cook gently for about 10 minutes with 1/2 cup broth.

7. In a second saucepan, toast the rice with the remaining onion for 2 minutes.

8. Add 5 cups hot broth in five 1-cup additions, one every 2–3 minutes.

9. Halfway through cooking, add the peas and pancetta.

10. Continue until the rice is al dente and looser than an ordinary risotto, about 16–18 minutes total.

11. Turn off the heat.

12. Add the remaining 3/4 cup broth, the remaining butter, Parmigiano, parsley, salt, and pepper.

13. Stir vigorously and rest for 1 minute.

Service

Serve in bowls with a creamy, slightly brothy consistency.

Chef's note

Risi e bisi should be looser than risotto but thicker than soup. Do not let the rice absorb all of the broth.

title: Cuttlefish-ink Risotto
instructions:
Cuttlefish-ink Risotto

Venetian risotto with cuttlefish, cuttlefish ink, white wine, fish broth, and parsley.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

1 1/2 cups Vialone Nano or Carnaroli rice
1 1/3 lb cleaned cuttlefish, cut into pieces
about 2 tsp cuttlefish ink
1 white onion, finely chopped
4 1/4 cups hot fish broth
4 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp dry white wine
1/4 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
3/4 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Keep the fish broth at a gentle simmer.

2. Heat the olive oil in a saucepan.

3. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes.

4. Add the cuttlefish and sauté for 2–3 minutes.

5. Add the rice and toast for 1–2 minutes.

6. Pour in the white wine and let it evaporate.

7. Reserve 1/4 cup broth for the cuttlefish ink and add the remaining 4 cups broth in four 1-cup additions, at the start and after 4, 8, and 12 minutes.

8. After 8–10 minutes, dissolve the cuttlefish ink in 1/4 cup hot broth.

9. Add it to the rice and stir thoroughly.

10. Continue cooking to about 18 minutes total, stirring frequently after the final broth addition.

11. Season with salt.

12. Turn off the heat and add the parsley.

Service

title: Amarone Risotto
instructions:
Amarone Risotto

Vialone Nano risotto with Amarone reduction, butter, and aged Monte Veronese.

instructions:
Feltre-style Rice and Beans

Venetian rice and beans with borlotti beans, pork rind, lard, onion, garlic, sage, and tomato.

8. Add the rice and most of the salt.

Serve hot and creamy, but not completely dry.

Chef's note

The rice cooks directly in the bean broth, absorbing starch, rendered lard, and the flavor of the pork rind.

Soft pumpkin gnocchi with melted butter and smoked ricotta.

1. Cut the pumpkin into large pieces and remove the seeds and fibers.

2. Steam until even the skin is tender, or roast at 350°F for about 30 minutes.

3. Cool.

4. Scoop out the flesh and mash with a fork.

5. Add the egg.

6. Work in the flour gradually until the mixture is creamy and sticky rather than firm enough to roll.

7. Bring the salted cooking water to a boil.

8. Dip a teaspoon into the boiling water.

9. Scoop small portions of batter and drop them directly into the water.

10. Once each gnocco floats, cook for 1 additional minute.

11. Lift out with a slotted spoon.

12. Melt the butter over low heat.

Service

Chef's note

Keep the mixture soft and sticky. Too much flour makes the gnocchi heavy and masks the pumpkin flavor.

Casunziei Ampezzani

Cortina half-moon pasta filled with beet and potato, finished with butter, poppy seeds, and smoked ricotta.

title: Venetian Pasta and Beans
instructions:
Venetian Pasta and Beans

Venetian bean soup with Lamon beans, clove-studded onion, egg noodles, and extra-virgin olive oil.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

3 cups fresh Lamon beans or 1 cup dried beans
1 whole peeled onion
6 whole cloves
6 1/3 cups water for cooking, plus 4 1/4 cups to adjust the soup
2 tsp coarse salt
about 1/2 lb dry egg tagliolini or ditalini
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. If using dried beans, soak them in cold water for at least 6 hours.

2. Drain and rinse.

3. Put the beans in a pressure cooker with the measured cooking water and coarse salt.

4. Bring to full pressure over high heat.

5. Reduce the heat to low and cook for 40 minutes.

6. Let the pressure release completely before opening.

7. Pass the beans and their liquid through a food mill into a large pot, removing the skins completely.

8. Stud the onion with the cloves.

9. Add it to the bean puree with about 4 1/4 cups hot water.

10. Bring to a boil and taste for salt.

11. If using tagliolini, break them into short pieces.

12. Add the pasta and cook until al dente, stirring often.

13. Remove the onion and cloves.

Service

Serve hot or warm with extra-virgin olive oil and black pepper.

Chef's note

Passing the beans through a food mill removes the skins and creates the characteristic velvety texture. Cook the pasta directly in the bean puree.

Venetian Macaroni Pasticcio

Cjarsons

instructions:
Mlinci with Chicken Supeta

Baked Friulian mlinci served with long-cooked chicken, onion, marjoram, white wine, and tomato sauce.

1 1/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Knead the flour, eggs, olive oil, herbs, and salt into a firm, smooth dough.

2. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.

3. Roll the dough thin.

4. Lay on a floured baking sheet.

5. Bake at 400°F for 10 minutes, until dry and lightly colored.

6. Cool and break into irregular pieces.

7. For the supeta, heat the olive oil in a large pot.

8. Brown the hen on all sides for 10 minutes.

9. Pour in the wine and let it evaporate.

10. Add the onions and cook for 8 minutes.

11. Add the marjoram, salt, and pepper.

12. Pour in the broth.

13. Cover partially and cook over low heat for about 3 hours.

14. Remove the hen, debone it, and cut the meat into pieces.

15. Return the meat to the sauce.

16. Add the tomato paste and breadcrumbs.

17. Cook for another 10 minutes, until thick.

18. Blanch the mlinci in boiling water for 1–2 minutes or soften them with a little hot broth before serving.

Serve the mlinci with generous chicken supeta.

The mlinci are dried in the oven first and rehydrated only at serving, allowing them to absorb the chicken sauce without falling apart.

Friulian Pasta and Beans

Friulian pasta and bean soup with borlotti beans, potatoes, vegetables, sage, rosemary, and bay.

instructions:
Trieste Jota

Trieste bean-and-sauerkraut soup with potatoes, smoked pancetta, caraway, and bay.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

about 3 cups precooked sauerkraut

about 1 cup diced smoked pancetta
3 garlic cloves, minced
1/4 cup olive oil, divided
2 tbsp flour
1 bay leaf
1 tsp caraway seeds

Preparation

1. Soak the beans in cold water for 12 hours.

2. Drain and rinse.

3. Heat half of the olive oil in a large pot.

4. Add half of the garlic and cook for 1 minute.

5. Add the pancetta, potatoes, and beans.

6. Sauté for 5 minutes.

7. Pour in the water.

8. Add most of the salt.

9. Bring to a boil and cook for 90 minutes.

10. In a second pot, combine the sauerkraut, caraway, and bay leaf.

11. Add just enough water to cover and cook until almost completely absorbed.

12. Heat the remaining olive oil in a skillet.

13. Add the remaining garlic and flour.

14. Cook, stirring, until the roux turns deep brown without burning.

15. Add the sauerkraut and stir.

16. Pass half of the cooked beans through a food mill.

17. Combine the bean puree, whole beans, potatoes, and sauerkraut.

18. Cook everything together for another 30 minutes.

19. Adjust with the remaining salt and pepper.

Service

Rest for at least 15 minutes before serving. It is even better reheated the next day.

Chef's note

Jota should be very thick. Pureeing half of the beans binds the soup without requiring additional flour.

1. Trim and wash the spinach thoroughly.

2. Melt the butter in a large pot.

3. Add the garlic and cook for 1–2 minutes.

4. Add the chopped spinach and cook until completely wilted, about 5 minutes.

5. Remove the garlic.

6. Pour in the hot broth and bring to a boil.

7. Combine the cornmeal and flour.

8. Slowly stream the flours into the broth while whisking rapidly to prevent lumps.

9. Add the salt.

10. Reduce the heat and cook for 20–30 minutes, stirring every few minutes.

11. If the polenta becomes too thick before it is fully cooked, add more hot broth in small amounts.

Service

Serve very hot and creamy in bowls.

Chef's note

Paparot should remain softer than sliceable polenta. Adjust with hot broth during cooking to maintain a flowing consistency.

8. Meanwhile, boil the barley in salted water for 20–25 minutes, until nearly tender. Drain and reserve.

9. In a skillet, brown the pancetta in the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil for 5–6 minutes.

10. Remove the bay leaf and pork rind from the bean pot.

11. Pass the carrot, celery, onion, and about one-third of the beans through a food mill.

12. Return the puree to the pot.

13. Add the barley, potatoes, and browned pancetta.

14. Cook for another 20 minutes.

15. Season with salt and pepper.

Cooking the barley separately helps it retain texture while the bean base remains creamy.

Paularo Agnolotti

South Tyrolean bread dumplings with Speck, eggs, and milk, served in meat broth.

Canederli in Broth

Trentino bread dumplings with fresh sausage, Speck, Trentingrana, and herbs, served in vegetable broth.

2 cups dry breadcrumbs
1 cup finely grated Trentingrana

Preparation

1. Put the cold water in a pot with all of the cleaned, chopped vegetables, optional bay leaf, peppercorns, and unpeeled garlic.

2. Bring to a boil.

3. Add the coarse salt and parsley.

4. Cover and cook for about 90 minutes.

7. Pour in the milk and let it soak for 10 minutes.

8. Add the eggs, sausage, Speck, Trentingrana, salt, pepper, and parsley.

9. Mix by hand.

10. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.

11. Add the breadcrumbs.

12. If the mixture is still too soft to shape, add flour 1 tablespoon at a time.

13. With wet hands, form dumplings about the size of a small orange.

14. Bring the strained broth to a gentle simmer.

15. Cook the dumplings for about 15 minutes.

Service

Serve in bowls with plenty of broth and shaved Trentingrana.

Chef's note

Add flour only if absolutely necessary. Too much flour makes the dumplings heavy.

instructions:
Spinach Spätzle with Speck and Cream

South Tyrolean spinach spätzle with crisp Speck, cream, butter, nutmeg, and Parmigiano.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the spätzle
about 6 cups fresh spinach
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp water
2 large eggs
2 cups plus 2 tbsp flour
3/4 tsp fine salt

For the sauce
about 1 1/2 cups sliced Speck
1 cup plus 1 tbsp heavy cream
3 1/2 tbsp butter
1/4 tsp freshly grated nutmeg
1 tbsp finely grated Parmigiano
2/3 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

For cooking
4 1/4 qt water
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Wash the spinach.

2. Blanch it in boiling water for 2–3 minutes.

3. Drain, cool, and squeeze very dry.

4. Put the spinach, water, eggs, and salt in a blender.

5. Blend until smooth.

6. Add the flour.

7. Blend or stir until the batter is soft but thick enough to fall slowly from a spoon.

8. Bring the salted cooking water to a boil.

9. Press the batter into the water through a spätzle maker.

10. As soon as the spätzle rise to the surface, lift them out with a slotted spoon.

11. Melt about 1 tablespoon butter in a nonstick skillet.

12. Add the Speck and cook until crisp.

13. Add the remaining butter, cream, and nutmeg.

14. Season with salt and pepper and cook gently for 2–3 minutes.

15. Add the spätzle and toss for 1 minute.

Service

Divide among 4 plates and finish with Parmigiano.

Chef's note

Squeeze the spinach very dry. Excess water makes the batter too loose to work through the spätzle maker.

instructions:
Schlutzkrapfen

South Tyrolean rye-and-wheat half-moon pasta filled with spinach, ricotta, Grana, and chives, finished with melted butter.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the pasta
1 1/4 cups rye flour
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp wheat flour
1 large egg
3–4 tbsp warm water
1 tbsp oil
1/2 tsp fine salt

For the filling
about 1 cup cooked spinach or 6 cups fresh spinach
1/3 cup finely chopped onion
1/2 garlic clove
1 tbsp butter
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp ricotta
1 tbsp finely grated Grana
1 tbsp chopped chives
1 pinch freshly grated nutmeg
2/3 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

For finishing
4 tbsp melted butter
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp finely grated Grana
2 tbsp chopped chives

For cooking
4 1/4 qt water
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Combine the two flours and salt and form a well.

2. Mix the egg, warm water, and oil.

3. Pour into the center and knead for 8–10 minutes until uniform.

4. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.

5. Finely chop the spinach.

6. Melt the butter in a skillet and add the onion and garlic.

7. Cook for 5 minutes.

8. Add the spinach and sauté for 2 minutes.

9. Remove from the heat and add the ricotta, Grana, chives, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.

10. Cool completely.

11. Roll the pasta thin and cut rounds about 2 3/4 inches wide.

12. Put a portion of filling in the center.

13. Lightly moisten the edges with water, fold into a half-moon, and press to seal.

14. Bring the salted cooking water to a boil.

15. Cook for 3–4 minutes.

16. Drain gently.

Service

Finish with melted butter, Grana, and chives.

Chef's note

Rye dough is less elastic than all-wheat pasta. Do not roll it excessively thin or overfill the half-moons.

title: Tirtlen
instructions:
Tirtlen

South Tyrolean rye-and-wheat fried pastries filled with spinach, sour ricotta, or sauerkraut.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the dough
1 2/3 cups rye flour
1 2/3 cups wheat flour
1 tbsp oil
3/4–1 cup milk
3/4 tsp fine salt

For the filling
about 3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp spinach filling, sour ricotta, or cooked sauerkraut

For frying
4 1/4 cups peanut or other neutral oil

Preparation

1. Combine the rye flour, wheat flour, and salt.

2. Add the oil and 3/4 cup milk.

3. Knead for 8–10 minutes, adding more milk gradually only if needed.

4. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.

5. Roll the dough into a long log.

6. Cut into 16 equal slices.

7. Roll each slice into a thin round.

8. Put about 1 tablespoon of the chosen filling on half of the rounds.

9. Cover with the remaining rounds.

10. Press the edges firmly to seal.

11. Heat the frying oil to 350°F.

12. Fry in small batches for 2–3 minutes per side, until puffed and golden.

13. Drain on paper towels.

Service

Serve very hot.

Chef's note

Keep the filling dry. Wet spinach or sauerkraut can make the pastry open during frying.

12. Cover with the remaining squares and seal the edges firmly.

Preparation

1. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

2. In a bowl, whisk together the orange juice, mustard, olive oil, oregano, half of the salt, and half of the pepper.

3. Cut the potatoes into pieces about 1 1/4 inches wide.

5. Drain the potatoes, reserving the marinade.

8. Cut small slits in the lamb pieces.

9. Push a little of the garlic-parsley mixture into the slits.

10. Coat the lamb in the reserved marinade.

11. Arrange it over the potatoes.

12. Pour all remaining marinade into the pan.

13. Roast for about 1 hour, turning the lamb and potatoes every 20 minutes.

14. If the pan becomes too dry, add hot water in 1/4-cup portions.

15. Check that the potatoes are tender and the lamb is well browned.

Service

Rest for 10 minutes and serve hot.

Chef's note

The potatoes begin underneath the lamb, where they absorb the meat juices and the orange-mustard marinade as they roast.

Roman spring lamb braised with onion, cured ham fat, Frascati, and broth, finished off the heat with egg yolks, lemon, and Parmigiano.

1. Cut the oxtail through the joints into pieces about 2–3 inches long.

2. Heat the olive oil and cured ham fat in a very large pot.

3. Add the oxtail and brown for 10 minutes.

4. Add the onions, garlic, cloves, salt, and pepper.

5. Cook for another 5 minutes.

6. Pour in the wine and cook covered over high heat for 10 minutes.

7. Add the peeled tomatoes.

8. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover partially, and cook for 2–3 hours.

9. Check every 20–30 minutes and add hot water in 1/2-cup portions if needed.

10. Soak the raisins in warm water for 15 minutes and drain.

11. Clean the celery and boil for 10–15 minutes.

12. Blend it with about 1/2 cup of its cooking water.

13. Add the chocolate, raisins, and pine nuts.

14. Stir in one ladle of oxtail sauce.

15. Pour the celery mixture into the pot.

16. Continue cooking for 15–20 minutes, until the meat is tender but not falling apart.

17. Toast the breadcrumbs in a dry skillet for 3 minutes.

Service

Serve the oxtail with plenty of sauce and toasted breadcrumbs.

Chef's note

The oxtail is ready when tender but still attached to the bone. Overcooking causes the meat to disintegrate completely.

17. Add the liver.

Chef's note

The liver, heart, and lungs cook at different rates. Adding them in sequence keeps the liver tender while ensuring the lungs cook through.

title: Porchetta di Ariccia
instructions:
Porchetta di Ariccia

Ariccia-style rolled pork belly and loin with garlic, rosemary, fennel, black pepper, white wine, and crackling skin.

Yield: 12–16 servings

Ingredients

6 1/2 lb rectangular skin-on pork belly
2 2/3 lb pork loin
2 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt
1 tbsp whole black peppercorns
6 garlic cloves
1/3 cup chopped fresh rosemary
2 tbsp dried fennel seed and fronds
2/3 cup dry white wine
1 tbsp plus 2 tsp coarse salt for the skin
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp water for the roasting pan
kitchen twine

Preparation

1. Score the skin in a 3/4-inch diamond pattern, about 1/8 inch deep.

2. Score the meat side in a 1 1/4-inch grid about 3/8 inch deep.

3. Pound the peppercorns, garlic, half of the fine salt, rosemary, and fennel in a mortar.

4. Rub the mixture thoroughly over the meat side and into the cuts.

5. Distribute the remaining fine salt.

6. Place the pork loin in the center of the belly.

7. Roll tightly and tie with kitchen twine every 1 1/4 inches.

8. Dry the skin completely.

9. Rub it with the coarse salt.

10. Place on a rack over a tray, uncovered, and refrigerate for 12–24 hours.

11. Remove from the refrigerator 2 hours before roasting.

12. Brush away the coarse salt and dry the skin again.

13. Preheat a conventional oven to 300°F.

14. Put the measured water in the roasting pan beneath the rack for the first 2 hours.

15. Roast for about 5 hours total, rotating the porchetta halfway through.

16. Every hour, brush only the exposed meat ends with a little white wine, keeping the skin dry.

17. Check for an internal temperature of 180–185°F in the center.

18. Increase the oven to 445°F or switch to the broiler.

19. Cook for another 20–30 minutes, watching closely, until the skin is very crisp.

20. Rest for 30–40 minutes, loosely covering only the meat ends with foil and leaving the skin uncovered.

Service

Slice about 3/8 inch thick and serve hot or at room temperature.

Chef's note

Keep the skin dry for crisp crackling. Wine, water, or foil directly on the skin will soften it.

title: Baccalà alla Romana
instructions:
Baccalà alla Romana

Roman-style baked salt cod with tomato, potatoes, black olives, raisins, pine nuts, and oregano.

Ingredients

1 lb desalted salt cod

1 cup quartered baby potatoes
2/3 cup black olives
2 tbsp raisins
2 tbsp pine nuts
1 shallot, sliced
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided
2 tsp fresh oregano
2/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Soak the raisins in warm water for 15 minutes and drain.

2. Quarter the potatoes and keep them in cold water.

3. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a wide skillet.

4. Add the shallot and cook for 5 minutes.

5. Add the passata, 1 teaspoon oregano, and salt.

6. Cook for 10 minutes.

7. Bring a pot of water to a boil.

8. Blanch the potatoes for 2 minutes and drain.

9. Divide the salt cod into 4 pieces.

10. Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil in a skillet.

11. Sear the cod for about 30 seconds per side.

12. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

13. Spread a layer of sauce in a baking dish.

14. Add the cod, potatoes, and raisins.

15. Cover with the remaining sauce.

16. Bake for 30 minutes.

17. Toast the pine nuts in a dry skillet for 2 minutes.

18. Add the olives and pine nuts to the baking dish.

19. Continue baking for the final 10 minutes.

Service

Rest for 5 minutes and finish with fresh oregano.

Chef's note

Salt cod is already salty. Taste the sauce before adding salt and keep additional seasoning restrained.

Roman Cuttlefish with Peas

Cooking the cuttlefish and peas separately until nearly done keeps the peas green and the cuttlefish tender.

title: Carciofi alla Giudia
instructions:
Carciofi alla Giudia

Roman Jewish-style artichokes fried twice until crisp and opened like flowers.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

4 globe artichokes
1 lemon
6 1/3 cups cold water
4 1/4 cups peanut oil for frying
1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Fill a bowl with the cold water and lemon juice.

2. Remove the tough outer leaves from the artichokes.

3. Trim just the tips and shorten the stems, leaving about 1 1/2–2 inches attached.

4. Soak the artichokes in the acidulated water for 10 minutes.

5. Drain and dry extremely well.

6. Gently tap each artichoke upside down on the work surface to begin opening the leaves.

7. Heat the oil to about 300–320°F.

8. Holding one artichoke by the stem with tongs, lower the head into the oil and then release it.

9. Fry for 6–8 minutes, turning, until the heart is nearly tender.

10. Drain on paper towels with the stem facing upward.

11. Rest for 10 minutes.

12. Gently open the leaves with your fingers or lightly flatten the head.

13. Season inside and out with salt.

14. Increase the oil to 350°F.

15. Fry a second time for about 1 minute, until the leaves are very crisp.

Service

Drain well and serve immediately.

Chef's note

The first fry cooks the heart; the second crisps the leaves. Dry the artichokes completely before they enter hot oil.

Carciofi alla Romana

Roman artichokes stuffed with parsley, wild mint, garlic, anchovies, breadcrumbs, and Grana, then braised with olive oil and white wine.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

4 artichokes

3 oil-packed anchovy fillets
2 tbsp breadcrumbs
1 tbsp finely grated Grana
1 garlic clove
1 lemon
6 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
3 tbsp dry white wine
3/4 cup water
3/4 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Prepare a bowl of cold water acidulated with the lemon juice.

2. Trim the artichokes, removing tough outer leaves and tips while leaving 1 1/2–2 inches of stem.

3. Place them in the acidulated water.

4. Finely chop the parsley, mint, garlic, and anchovies.

5. Mix with the breadcrumbs, Grana, about 1/3 teaspoon salt, and pepper.

6. Drain and dry the artichokes.

7. Gently spread the leaves.

8. Pack the filling into the heart and between the leaves.

9. Press the artichokes gently back into shape.

10. Stand them stem-up in a snug saucepan.

11. Add the olive oil, water, and wine.

12. Add the remaining salt.

13. Cover and bring to a moderate boil.

14. Cook for 20–25 minutes from the boil, until a knife enters the heart easily.

15. Uncover for the final 3–5 minutes to reduce the braising liquid.

Service

Serve hot or warm with the pan juices.

Chef's note

Use a saucepan that holds the artichokes closely together so they stay upright and retain their filling while braising.

Arista alla Fiorentina

Resting the pork in the pot redistributes its juices and lets it absorb the aromatics without continued aggressive cooking.

Bistecca alla Fiorentina

3. Pat the meat dry.

5. Cook the first side for about 5 minutes without piercing the meat.

6. Turn once with tongs.

7. Season the cooked side with salt.

8. Cook the second side for another 5 minutes.

9. Salt the second side.

10. For especially thick steaks, stand them briefly on the bone for 2–3 minutes.

11. Remove from the grill and rest for 5 minutes.

Finish with black pepper and optional lemon wedges.

Chef's note

Do not pierce or press the steaks. Intense heat forms the crust while the center remains red and juicy.

instructions:
Peposo All'imprunetina

Tuscan beef stew cooked slowly in Chianti with abundant black pepper and garlic.

6 1/3 cups Chianti or other Tuscan red wine
2 tbsp coarsely crushed black peppercorns
6 garlic cloves, crushed
2 tsp fine salt
8 slices toasted Tuscan-style bread for serving

Preparation

1. Heat a heavy pot over medium-high heat.

2. Add the beef without oil and brown it in its own fat for 10–12 minutes.

3. Pour in enough red wine to cover the meat generously.

4. Add the pepper, garlic, and salt.

5. Bring just to a simmer.

6. Cover with the lid slightly ajar.

7. Cook over very low heat or in a 300°F oven for about 3 hours.

8. Stir every 30 minutes.

9. If needed, add more wine or a little hot water to keep the meat nearly covered during the first part of cooking.

10. During the final hour, uncover partially to concentrate the sauce.

11. Cook until the beef is extremely tender and the sauce thick and creamy.

Service

Serve over toasted Tuscan-style bread.

Chef's note

Peposo needs no soffritto. Wine, pepper, and very long cooking transform the beef and collagen directly into an intense sauce.

Tuscan Braised Wild Boar

Preparation

1. Put the wild boar in a nonreactive container.

2. Add 1 sliced onion, 1 carrot, 1 celery stalk, 2 bay leaves, and 1 rosemary sprig.

3. Add 1/2 cup olive oil and toss thoroughly.

4. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 days, turning the meat once each day.

5. Drain the boar and discard the marinade vegetables and herbs.

6. Finely chop the remaining onion, carrot, celery, and garlic.

7. Heat the remaining olive oil in a heavy pot.

8. Add the chopped vegetables with the remaining bay and rosemary and cook for 8 minutes.

9. Add the boar and brown over high heat for 10–12 minutes.

10. Pour in the red wine and cook for 5 minutes.

11. Reduce the heat and cook slowly for about 90 minutes.

12. Once the liquid has mostly reduced, add the tomato, salt, and pepper.

13. Continue for another 45–60 minutes, adding hot broth in 1/2-cup portions if needed.

14. Thirty minutes before the end, add the black olives and nutmeg.

Service

Remove the bay and rosemary and serve very hot.

Chef's note

The long aromatic marinade softens the wild character of the boar. Add the olives only during the final half-hour so they keep their texture.

Tuscan Scottiglia

Maremma mixed-meat stew with soffritto, red wine, tomato, and toasted bread.

Preparation

1. Heat the olive oil in a heavy or clay pot.

2. Add the soffritto and bay leaves.

3. Cook over medium heat for 7–8 minutes.

4. Add the meats, leaving bone-in pieces whole and cutting boneless meats into large cubes.

5. Brown over high heat for 10–15 minutes, turning the pieces 2–3 times.

6. Pour in the red wine.

7. Cook until almost completely evaporated.

8. Reduce the heat.

9. Add the tomatoes, salt, and pepper.

10. Cover with the lid slightly ajar.

11. Cook over low heat for about 2 hours, stirring every 20 minutes.

12. Add a little hot water if needed to keep the bottom from catching.

13. Toast the bread and rub with garlic if desired.

Serve the scottiglia over or alongside the toasted bread.

Chef's note

Use meats with different textures. Bone-in pieces deepen the sauce, while boneless meat softens slightly into the stew.

Rabbit with Vernaccia

1 rabbit, about 2 2/3 lb, cleaned and cut into pieces

Preparation

1. Rinse the rabbit briefly if needed and pat very dry.

2. Dredge lightly in flour and shake off the excess.

3. Heat 3 tablespoons olive oil in a wide saucepan.

4. Brown the rabbit for 2–3 minutes per side.

5. Pour in the Vernaccia and let it almost completely evaporate.

6. Transfer the rabbit to a plate.

7. Reduce the heat and add the remaining olive oil and onions.

8. Cook for 4 minutes.

9. Return the rabbit to the pan.

10. Add 1/2 cup broth, cover, and cook over low heat for about 40 minutes, adding more hot broth in small amounts if needed.

11. Uncover, add the olives, salt, and pepper, and cook for another 20 minutes.

12. In a bowl, beat the eggs, lemon juice, and parsley.

13. Turn off the heat.

14. Slowly whisk 1/4 cup hot pan juices into the egg mixture.

15. Pour the tempered sauce over the rabbit and stir for 1–2 minutes without boiling.

Service

Serve immediately with the creamy sauce.

title: Baccalà alla Livornese
instructions:
Baccalà alla Livornese

Livorno-style salt cod, fried until crisp and finished in tomato, onion, garlic, and parsley sauce.

instructions:
Cacciucco alla Livornese

Livorno fish stew with octopus, shellfish, rock fish, crustaceans, tomato, red wine, and garlic toast.

Preparation

1. Remove the heads from the rock fish and brown them in a clay pot with half of the olive oil, 1 garlic clove, and 3 sage leaves for 5 minutes.

2. Add the water and cook for 20 minutes.

3. Strain the broth carefully and reserve.

4. Clean and portion all fish and shellfish.

5. Heat the remaining olive oil in the same pot.

6. Add the celery, carrot, onion, remaining garlic, sage, and chile.

7. Cook for 8 minutes.

8. Pour in the red wine and let it evaporate.

9. Add the passata and strained broth.

10. Bring to a boil.

11. Add the octopus and cook for 20 minutes.

12. Add the squid, cuttlefish, and baby octopus and cook for 10–15 minutes.

13. Add the rock fish, stargazer, weever fish, monkfish, and dogfish and cook another 10 minutes.

14. Add the tomato paste, shrimp, mantis shrimp, and mussels.

15. Cook for 4–5 minutes, until the mussels open. Discard any that remain closed.

16. Season with salt and pepper.

17. Toast the bread and rub with garlic.

Service

Place the toast in bowls and ladle over the fish, shellfish, and abundant broth.

Chef's note

Add the seafood in order of cooking time so the crustaceans and delicate fish do not become tough.

5. Add the sturdier fish pieces, beginning with the eel.

7. Pour in the white wine and let it evaporate.

8. Add the bay leaves and tomato paste.

10. Season with salt and pepper.

11. Add the remaining olive oil, garlic, sage, and rosemary.

12. Add about 1 1/4 cups wine and the juice of half a lemon.

13. Cover and cook over moderate heat for 45–60 minutes, turning regularly.

14. Remove the guinea fowl and strain the pan juices.

15. Return the meat to the pan.

16. Add the strained juices and liver sauce.

Umbrian Porchetta

Preparation

1. Open the pork flat with the skin side down.

2. Score or butterfly thicker areas to create an even thickness.

3. Finely chop the garlic, wild fennel, and rosemary.

4. Mix with the coarse salt and black pepper.

5. Spread the mixture evenly over the meat and massage thoroughly.

6. Drizzle with the olive oil.

7. Roll tightly starting from the loin side.

8. Tie firmly with kitchen twine every 1 1/4–1 1/2 inches.

9. Place the porchetta on a rack inside a large roasting pan with the skin facing upward.

10. Preheat the oven to 425°F.

11. Roast for 30 minutes.

12. Reduce the oven to 330°F.

13. Continue roasting for about 3 hours.

14. Every 45 minutes, baste the skin lightly with some of the rendered fat from the pan.

15. Verify that the center exceeds 170°F.

16. Rest for 20 minutes.

Chef's note

The initial high heat starts crisping the skin, while the long lower-temperature phase cooks the large roast evenly.

title: Umbrian Roast Suckling Pig
instructions:
Umbrian Roast Suckling Pig

Umbrian suckling pig roasted with garlic, rosemary, wild fennel, and crisp skin.

Yield: 8–10 servings

Ingredients

1 cleaned suckling pig, about 11 lb, opened flat
8 garlic cloves
2/3 cup chopped fresh rosemary
1/2 cup chopped wild fennel
2 tbsp coarse salt
1 tbsp freshly ground black pepper
1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil
1 cup plus 1 tbsp dry white wine

Preparation

1. Dry the pig thoroughly inside and out.

2. Finely chop the garlic, rosemary, and fennel.

3. Mix with most of the salt, black pepper, and olive oil.

4. Rub the mixture inside the cavity and over exposed meat, avoiding excessive oil on the skin.

5. Tie the pig if needed to maintain a compact shape.

6. Refrigerate uncovered for 12 hours to dry the skin.

7. Remove from the refrigerator 1 hour before roasting.

8. Preheat the oven to 425°F.

9. Rub the skin with the remaining coarse salt.

10. Roast for 30 minutes.

11. Reduce the oven to 320°F.

12. Pour the wine into the roasting pan, not over the skin.

13. Continue roasting for about 3 hours, rotating the pan every 45 minutes.

14. Add a little water to the pan if needed to prevent the juices from burning.

15. For crisper skin, increase the oven to 445°F for the final 15–20 minutes.

16. Verify that the thickest meat reaches at least 170°F.

17. Rest for 30 minutes with the skin uncovered.

Service

Portion and serve with defatted pan juices.

Chef's note

Do not baste the skin during roasting. Moisture prevents a crisp crust from forming.

Umbrian Roast Goose

Umbrian roast goose with sage, rosemary, garlic, white wine, and potatoes.

Yield: 8 servings

1 cup plus 1 tbsp dry white wine
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
2 1/2 tsp fine salt
2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
2 cups hot water or broth

Preparation

1. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

2. Pat the goose very dry.

3. Finely chop 3 garlic cloves, 8 sage leaves, and 2 rosemary sprigs.

4. Mix with half of the salt and pepper.

5. Rub the mixture inside the cavity and under the skin where possible.

6. Season the exterior with the remaining salt and pepper.

7. Place the goose on a rack over a roasting pan.

8. Roast for 45 minutes.

9. Carefully remove some of the rendered fat from the pan.

10. Cut the potatoes into large pieces and toss with the olive oil and remaining garlic, sage, and rosemary.

11. Arrange them in the pan beneath the goose.

12. Pour the wine into the pan.

13. Continue roasting for 90–120 minutes, turning the potatoes every 30 minutes.

14. Add water or broth in 1/2-cup portions if the pan becomes dry.

15. Verify an internal temperature of at least 165°F in the thickest part of the thigh.

16. Rest for 20 minutes.

Service

Carve the goose and serve with the potatoes and defatted pan juices.

Chef's note

Removing some rendered fat during cooking prevents the potatoes from frying in an excessive layer of goose fat.

Salt Cod with Black Truffle

Umbrian salt cod with fresh black-truffle cream, extra-virgin olive oil, and parsley.

4. Heat half of the olive oil in a skillet.

Service

Chef's note

Add the truffle away from direct heat to preserve its aroma. Salt cod usually needs very little additional salt.

Pecora alla Callara

Abruzzo-style sheep stew slowly cooked with white wine, tomato, onion, garlic, celery, carrot, and herbs.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

6 1/2 lb sheep meat, preferably shoulder and leg, cut into 2–2 1/2-inch pieces

about 6 1/2 cups chopped ripe tomatoes

Preparation

1. Trim only the thickest exterior fat from the meat.

2. Put the meat in a very large pot.

3. Add the wine and enough cold water to cover completely.

4. Bring slowly to a boil.

5. Skim fat and impurities thoroughly from the surface during the first 20–30 minutes.

6. Continue the initial cooking for 1 hour.

7. Add the onions, garlic, carrot, celery, bay, rosemary, sage, thyme, chile, and tomatoes.

8. Add the salt and pepper.

9. Reduce the heat to very low.

10. Cook for about 3 hours, stirring every 30 minutes.

11. Add hot water in 1-cup portions only if the meat is no longer nearly covered.

12. Continue until the meat is extremely tender and the liquid rich but still brothy.

Service

Serve very hot in large bowls with rustic bread.

Chef's note

The initial skimming is essential because it removes some of the sheep's stronger rendered fat and gives a cleaner broth.

title: Tacchino alla Canzanese
instructions:
Tacchino alla Canzanese

Abruzzo-style turkey slowly cooked with its bones, garlic, bay, and pepper, then chilled in its own natural gelatin.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

13 lb whole turkey
4 unpeeled garlic cloves
4 bay leaves
2 tsp black peppercorns
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp coarse salt
3 1/4 qt water

Preparation

1. Remove the turkey legs.

2. Debone the body with a thin flexible knife, reserving all bones.

3. Spread the body meat evenly and season with half of the salt.

4. Re-form the turkey and tie securely with kitchen twine.

5. Break the bones into large pieces.

6. Arrange them in the bottom of a very large oven-safe pot.

7. Place the legs and tied turkey on top.

8. Add the remaining salt, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns.

9. Pour in the water.

10. Roast in a preheated 400°F oven for 1 hour.

11. Reduce the oven to 350°F.

12. Continue cooking for about 3 hours, turning the meat every 45 minutes.

13. Remove the legs and strip the meat from the bones.

14. Remove the twine and skin from the turkey.

15. Transfer all of the meat to a rectangular container.

16. Strain the hot broth very thoroughly.

17. Pour it over the meat until covered.

18. Cool to room temperature.

19. Refrigerate for at least 12 hours, until the broth sets into a firm natural gelatin.

Service

Slice and serve cold with the gelatin.

Chef's note

The gelatin forms naturally from collagen extracted from the bones during the long cooking; no added gelatin is required.

Pallotte Cacio e Ova

3. Add the passata and salt.

4. Cook over low heat for 20 minutes.

5. Finely process the bread crumb.

6. Transfer to a bowl.

7. Add the Pecorino, eggs, parsley, pepper, and salt.

8. Mix by hand until uniform.

9. Form 15 compact balls.

10. Heat the sunflower oil to 330°F.

11. Fry a few balls at a time for about 2 minutes, turning until evenly golden.

13. Transfer the fried balls to the tomato sauce.

14. Simmer over low heat for another 10 minutes.

15. Remove the garlic.

Service

Serve very hot with plenty of sauce.

Chef's note

The balls should be firm before frying. Their final simmer in tomato softens them without allowing them to fall apart.

instructions:
Lamb with Lampascioni

Roast lamb with lampascioni bulbs, white wine, garlic, rosemary, and a Pecorino-breadcrumb crust.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

3 1/4 lb lamb, cut into pieces
about 3 cups cleaned lampascioni bulbs
2 cups fresh rustic breadcrumbs
1/2 cup finely grated Pecorino
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp dry white wine
3 garlic cloves
1 rosemary sprig
1/2 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
6 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
1/4 tsp ground chile
1 cup hot water, available during cooking

Preparation

1. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

2. Heat 1/4 cup olive oil in a large deep roasting pan that can also go on the stovetop.

3. Add the garlic and lamb.

4. Brown the lamb on all sides for 10–12 minutes.

5. Remove the garlic when golden.

6. Pour in the wine and let it evaporate for 3 minutes.

7. Add the rosemary, salt, and chile.

8. Add 1/2 cup hot water.

9. Transfer to the oven and roast for at least 1 hour.

10. Meanwhile, clean the lampascioni and cut a shallow cross in the base of each.

11. Boil in salted water for 15 minutes.

12. Drain.

13. Mix the breadcrumbs, Pecorino, parsley, and a small pinch of chile.

14. When the lamb is nearly tender, add the lampascioni.

15. Scatter the breadcrumb mixture over the top.

16. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil.

17. Bake for another 20 minutes.

18. Moisten the crust with 2–3 tablespoons of the pan juices.

19. Broil for 2–3 minutes, until golden.

Service

Rest for 5 minutes and serve hot.

Chef's note

Boiling the lampascioni first reduces their bitterness and lets them finish cooking with the lamb without falling apart.

title: Pampanella Molisana
instructions:
Pampanella Molisana

San Martino in Pensilis-style pork seasoned with garlic, sweet and hot red pepper, and white-wine vinegar, then slowly roasted.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

2 1/4 lb pork, preferably loin, shoulder, or meaty ribs
3 tbsp sweet paprika or sweet red-pepper powder
1 tbsp hot paprika or hot red-pepper powder
4 garlic cloves, minced
4 tbsp white-wine vinegar, plus 1/2 cup for finishing
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
1/2 cup water

Preparation

1. If the pork is in one piece, cut almost all the way through into slices about 3/4 inch thick, leaving the bottom attached like a book.

2. Mix the sweet pepper, hot pepper, garlic, and salt.

3. Rub the mixture over every surface of the pork and into the cuts.

4. Drizzle with 4 tablespoons vinegar.

5. Cover and refrigerate for 4 hours.

6. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

7. Arrange the pork in a roasting pan.

8. Pour the water into the bottom of the pan.

9. Cover the meat with damp parchment and then foil, or with clean grape leaves if available.

10. Roast for 90 minutes.

11. Remove the covering.

12. Drain excess water and fat from the pan.

13. Sprinkle the pork with the remaining 1/2 cup vinegar.

14. Return to the oven uncovered for 20–30 minutes, until the red coating is dry and firmly set.

Service

Rest for 10 minutes and serve hot or at room temperature.

Chef's note

The final vinegar is essential. Adding it after the covered phase brightens the rich pork instead of allowing the acidity to disappear during the long roast.

title: Baccalà Arracanato
instructions:
Baccalà Arracanato

Molise-style baked salt cod with rustic breadcrumbs, black olives, pine nuts, raisins, cherry tomatoes, oregano, and white wine.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

1 1/3 lb desalted salt cod, skinned and deboned
about 5 cups fresh rustic breadcrumbs
2/3 cup pine nuts or chopped walnuts
1/2 cup raisins
1 1/3 cups pitted black olives, chopped
2 cups halved cherry tomatoes
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp dry white wine
3 bay leaves
1 tbsp dried oregano
1 garlic clove, minced
1 small onion, finely chopped
1/3 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil
1 tsp fennel seeds
1/3 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Soak the raisins in very hot water for 10 minutes.

2. Transfer them to warm water for another 30 minutes.

3. Drain and dry thoroughly.

4. Mix the breadcrumbs, olives, pine nuts, raisins, garlic, onion, parsley, oregano, fennel seeds, salt, and pepper.

5. Preheat the oven to 375°F.

6. Grease the bottom of a baking dish with 2 tablespoons olive oil.

7. Arrange the bay leaves over the bottom.

8. Cover with half of the breadcrumb mixture.

9. Arrange the salt cod pieces on top.

10. Add half of the tomatoes.

11. Cover with the remaining breadcrumb mixture.

12. Decorate with the remaining tomatoes.

13. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil.

14. Bake for 10 minutes.

15. Pour the white wine around the edges of the dish without washing away the topping.

16. Continue baking for another 20 minutes.

Service

Rest for 5 minutes and serve hot.

Chef's note

Add the wine after the first 10 minutes so the breadcrumb topping begins to toast before it is moistened.

title: Pezzata di Capracotta
instructions:
Pezzata di Capracotta

Capracotta-style sheep slowly cooked with potatoes, celery, tomato, and chile.

Yield: 30–40 servings

Ingredients

1 sheep, 33–44 lb, trimmed of excess fat and cut into large pieces
4 large potatoes, cut into pieces
1 celery stalk, cut into 3 pieces
4 ripe tomatoes, halved
1 hot chile
about 8 gal cold water, or enough to cover the meat by at least 4 inches in the cauldron
1/2 cup coarse salt

Preparation

1. Put the meat in a large tinned cauldron or very large stockpot.

2. Add cold water until it stands at least 4 inches above the meat.

3. Add the salt.

4. Bring slowly to a boil.

5. During the first stage of cooking, remove all foam and rendered fat from the surface very carefully.

6. Continue skimming until the broth is relatively clear.

7. Add the potatoes, celery, tomatoes, and chile.

8. Cover partially.

9. Cook over low heat for at least 4 hours, stirring gently every 30 minutes.

10. During cooking, do not add more water unless the meat threatens to become completely uncovered.

11. Continue until the meat is extremely tender and the liquid has reduced to a loose, creamy broth.

Service

Serve very hot in deep bowls with the reduced broth and potatoes.

Chef's note

The long initial skimming removes excess fat and stronger aromas. The potatoes then help naturally thicken the final broth.
